### Macs a parent or an organisation looks after
This Mac can now be set up as someone else's to look after. On first run it asks what kind of device it is — your own, a child's, or one belonging to an organisation — and a child or organisation device takes its rules from the person managing it rather than from whoever is sitting at the keyboard. The Profile screen says plainly who that is, and signing back in after a sign-out offers the same three paths instead of only the personal one.
A managed Mac also has to finish its setup: Accessibility, notifications and Safe Internet are all required before it can be used, and it cannot be quit while it is enforcing. Uninstall protection switches itself on, so nobody has to remember to.
### The rules a parent or administrator sets are now enforced here
Everything set on the parent or organisation console reaches this Mac:
- whole apps and whole sites blocked together, so blocking YouTube covers the site as well as the app, and Telegram covers its web client - YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels and Facebook Reels, without blocking the rest of the site - WhatsApp's Updates tab and Telegram's search, in the apps and on the web - your own list of sites to block, with an exceptions list beside it - risky words rendered on a page, now in Discord and WhatsApp as well as browsers - the DNS filter level, and a lock on changing DNS settings
Changes land within a minute. When the console can reach the Mac directly they land in seconds.
### Fixes
The block screen now covers only the browser window it belongs to, rather than the whole display — a blocked site no longer looks like the Mac has been taken over. Repeatedly visiting one blocked site no longer starts closing tabs.
Only one copy of Kahf Guard runs at a time. Two could disagree about the current rules, and the older one would go on enforcing yesterday's.
The background helper no longer steals focus while you work.
